rulers.note: Map caption 'Kuyavia, held by Bolesław 1186–95'; killed at Mozgawa on 13 September 1195.

rulers.name: Mieszko III the Old

Mieszko is the researcher's reading because in 1198 he 'was compelled to cede Kuyavia to Casimir's sons'; the real holder of 1195-1198 is unknown.

Repair pass: the Kuyavia page names Inowrocław and Kruszwica among the region's towns, but Cliopatria's shape holds neither (the shape lies round Włocławek, Brześć Kujawski, Gostynin, Kutno, Łowicz and Toruń), so the disc is added; it overlaps no Greater Poland or Masovia shape. Area: the Kuyavia page infobox gives Total 5,989 km2 for the region (no year); Cliopatria's 6,844 km2 is a ratio of 1.14, the corrected shape (9,610 km2 by the gazetteer) 1.6, both within a factor of two.

region.text: the Kuyavia region, taken by Mieszko III on the death of Leszek of Masovia

ledger.note: 1186: Mieszko III the Old annexes Kuyavia and gives it to his son Bolesław. 'upon Leszek's death in 1186, he took the Kuyavia region and annexed it to his Duchy', then 'ceded the land to his son Bolesław' (undated); map caption 'Kuyavia, held by Bolesław 1186–95'. Cliopatria starts the duchy in 1188. Repair pass: the counterpart was duchy-of-masovia (where the land came from); it is now the annexer, as in the Masovia dossier's 1186 loss (counterpart duchy-of-greater-poland). The region adds the Inowrocław disc (see the keyframes).

region.text: Kuyavia, annexed 'to his Duchy' and held by Mieszko's son Bolesław

ledger.note: 1186: Kuyavia becomes Greater Poland's appanage. Mieszko III page: 'he took the Kuyavia region and annexed it to his Duchy' (the Greater Poland page: 'annexing Kuyavia', extending his control east to the Vistula), then 'ceded this land to his son Bolesław'; caption 'Kuyavia, held by Bolesław 1186–95'. The counterpart is the overlord, as in a vassal's own ledger. The Greater Poland dossier draws the same Cliopatria Kuyavia shape as its own direct land in 1186-1198 (its /ledger/4 gain, keyframes _1186 and _1188 and /ledger/11 loss to duchy-of-kuyavia), so the land is drawn twice until it turns its gain and loss into the mirror vassal_start and vassal_end and drops the Kuyavia union. Repair of reviewer finding 1.

13 September 1195: Bolesław of Kuyavia dies at Mozgawa. 'Battle of Mozgawa on 13 September 1195, where Mieszko himself was seriously injured' and his son 'Bolesław of Kuyavia died'. The page does not say who held Kuyavia next; Mieszko III again is the researcher's reading, since he cedes it in 1198. The Greater Poland page says 'following Bolesław's death in 1195, the region was again detached from Greater Poland', which the Mieszko III page does not support (it has Mieszko cede Kuyavia only in 1198).

1198: Mieszko III cedes Kuyavia to Casimir II's sons. 'In 1198, he was finally allowed to return to Lesser Poland, but was compelled to cede Kuyavia to Casimir's sons.' The Greater Poland page dates the cession to Konrad of Masovia to 1199 and has Kuyavia 'again detached' after Bolesław's death in 1195; the year here is the Mieszko III page's. Replaces the former 1198 rename (a change of ruling line); Greater Poland's mirror is its 1199 loss to duchy-of-kuyavia, which should become the vassal_end. Repair of reviewer finding 1.

region.text: Kuyavia, ceded to Duke Konrad of Masovia

ledger.note: 1199: Kuyavia passes to Konrad of Masovia, son of Casimir II. Greater Poland page: Mieszko 'was compelled to cede it to Duke Konrad of Masovia, son of Casimir II, in 1199'. The Mieszko III page has the cession to 'Casimir's sons' in 1198 and does not name Konrad or 1199; the Konrad I page (second page) has Konrad receive 'Masovia in 1199 and in 1205, the adjacent lands of Kuyavia as well', so the 1199 overlordship may be only a claim and the direct annexation 1205. The year is the Greater Poland page's; that Kuyavia was a tinted dependency of Masovia rather than a state of its own in 1199-1204 is the reviewer's and my reading (confidence 2). The counterpart is the overlord; the Masovia dossier has only the 1205 gain and needs the mirror vassal_start. Repair of reviewer finding 1.

1205: Konrad takes Kuyavia directly. 'In 1199, he received Masovia and in 1205, the adjacent lands of Kuyavia as well' (Konrad I of Masovia page). The dependency of 1199-1204 ends as the Masovia dossier records the direct gain (its /ledger/7, counterpart duchy-of-kuyavia).

region.text: the duchy's last Cliopatria shape (with the Inowrocław disc); the land joins Masovia

ledger.note: 1205: Konrad I adds Kuyavia to Masovia: 'in 1205, the adjacent lands of Kuyavia as well'. Cliopatria's Kuyavia row ends in 1205. Neither the Duchy of Kuyavia page nor the Mieszko III page dates an end; the Kuyavia page says Kuyavia was connected with Masovia and 'separated' from it in 1230. Kuyavia reappears as an independent duchy under Casimir I in 1230/1233 (Kuyavia page), which this dossier does not cover. Previously confidence 1 on the Masovia dossier's mirror alone; the Konrad I page now supplies the year.

wars.name: Battle of Mozgawa
belligerents: Kraków nobility backing Casimir II's sons (opponents not named by the page)
wars.outcome: Bloody battle on 13 September 1195: Mieszko III is seriously injured, his son Bolesław of Kuyavia dies and Mieszko withdraws to Kalisz; the page names no winner. Kuyavia stays in Piast hands until the 1198 cession.
wars.note: 'the local nobility preferred to see on the throne the minor sons of Casimir, Leszek the White and Konrad'; Mieszko's allies were 'Mieszko Tanglefoot and Jarosław of Opole' with Silesian troops. No land changed hands in the battle itself.

Page conflict: the Konrad I page puts Konrad's receipt of Kuyavia in 1205, the Greater Poland page in 1199, the Mieszko III page in 1198 ('Casimir's sons'); the Greater Poland page also has Kuyavia 'again detached' in 1195. (2) Capital: the Inowrocław disc (25 km, also takes in Kruszwica) is added to all three keyframes, which are now adjust; nothing overlaps Greater Poland's 1188 or Masovia's 1202 shapes.
